tagline.text: A turquoise lagoon and jump platform hidden among the mangroves

location.label: Location
location.text: An island off Caub village, Del Carmen, Siargao (by boat from Del Carmen Pier)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–October (mostly the dry season before the rains)

children.text: Sugba Lagoon is a clear lagoon tucked inside the mangrove forest of Del Carmen on western Siargao. Visitors come for the jump platform, kayaks and stand-up paddleboards, and it is popular as part of an island-hopping route that continues to Kawhagan Sandbar and Pamomo-an Beach.

Sugba Lagoon sits on an island off Caub village in the Del Carmen area on the western side of Siargao Island (sources give the island's name differently, such as Kangbangyo or Caob). From Del Carmen Pier, a bangka boat weaves through mangrove channels until a large welcome sign appears, and behind it lies emerald water ringed by hills. Because the lagoon is connected to the sea, the water is calm and clear, which makes it great for swimming and kayaking.

The lagoon's trademarks are the jump platform built over the water and a floating house moored in the middle of the lagoon. Photos of people leaping off the platform have become a staple of Siargao trips, and the floating house is a place to leave your things and rest. You can also rent kayaks, stand-up paddleboards and bamboo rafts to explore every corner of the lagoon.
Most travelers stay in General Luna and visit as a day trip. The ride from General Luna to Del Carmen by scooter or car takes about
40–45 minutes
, and the boat ride from the pier to the lagoon takes about
20–40 minutes
. Travel times differ between sources because they depend on the boat route and sea conditions, so it is best to confirm locally.

You can visit the lagoon alone, but the most popular option is a single boat that combines the mangrove viewing deck, Sugba Lagoon, Kawhagan Sandbar and Pamomo-an Beach. Because the boat is shared, the more people you have, the less each person pays. Fees and rules change every year, so check the latest announcements.

blocks.title: The jump platform and the hidden higher jump spot

children.text: The lagoon's main jump platform is where people queue up to pose for photos before leaping. If you arrive early, you can jump without waiting. Some reviews also mention a higher, quieter jump spot around a corner that you reach by kayak, so ask the staff first where it is and whether it is safe.

The floating house in the middle of the lagoon serves as a rest area and a place to store your belongings. Staff watch over bags, and some reviews say you can buy food and water there. Other reviews say almost nothing is sold at the lagoon, so it is safer to bring your own snacks and water. A table costs about
A regular kayak is listed at about

per hour. Whether gear is included depends on the tour, so check when you book.

The trip from the pier to the lagoon is a highlight in itself. The boat zigzags through the mangrove forest, and you can choose separate options such as the mangrove viewing deck or a walk through the mangroves. Some reviews also mention a small exhibit space at the ticket area that introduces the mangroves and the animals living there.
A white sandbar about
20 minutes

by boat from Sugba Lagoon. It is fully exposed at low tide, which makes it good for walking, and it is known as a drone-photo spot. A small wooden hut and a local eatery make it a frequent lunch stop on tours.

A beach that tours often visit as the last stop. It is described as having opened to the public in October 2019, and its strengths are unspoiled sand and clear water. There are few facilities, so plan mainly on swimming and relaxing.

If you go in on the first boat, you can take photos before the crowds arrive. One reviewer's boat was the second to arrive, and a tour group showed up only a few minutes later. If you want a quiet lagoon, leaving early in the morning is the most effective approach.

items.title: Half-day lagoon trip
items.subtitle: Sugba Lagoon only, on the first boat

children.text: Leave General Luna by scooter or pickup vehicle. The trip to Del Carmen takes about
40–45 minutes
Take the first boat from Del Carmen Pier. There may already be a queue, so it is best to arrive a little earlier. Pay the boat fee and environmental fee at the ticket area.
Ride the bangka through the mangrove channels to the lagoon. Take photos in front of the welcome sign at the entrance and leave your belongings at the floating house.
Jump from the platform before the crowds arrive, then paddle once around the lagoon by kayak or paddleboard.
Keep within the lagoon's stay limit (about
3 hours
) and take the boat back to the pier.
Have lunch near the pier or back in General Luna.
If you cannot spare a whole day, this half-day trip to the lagoon alone is the simplest option. Reviews say a boat holds up to six people, so gather a group and split the fee.
Leave your General Luna accommodation. If you book a tour, hotel pickup is included.
Board the boat at Del Carmen Pier. The full route combines all the stops on one boat.
Look down at the channels winding through the forest from the mangrove viewing deck.
Enjoy jumping and kayaking at Sugba Lagoon.
Have lunch at Kawhagan Sandbar and walk along the sandbar. At low tide the sandbar is exposed widely.
Swim and relax at Pamomo-an Beach.
Return to the pier before dark. Tour boats usually get back to General Luna before sunset.
The full route has the highest boat fee but lets you see everything in one trip. The stops and their order differ between operators, so confirm the stops and whether lunch is included when you book.
There are direct flights from Manila (MNL) to Siargao Sayak Airport (IAO). Routes and times vary by airline, so check before booking.
You can also connect through Cebu (CEB). From Siargao Airport, you travel to General Luna by car or van.
Del Carmen is on the opposite (western) side of the island from General Luna, so you have to cross the island.

items.title: From General Luna to Del Carmen Pier

children.text: Riding a rented scooter yourself takes about
40–45 minutes
. Daily rental fees vary between reviews, with some listing around
, so confirm locally. Reviews say parking at the pier is free.
If you book a tour, hotel pickup and the transfer to the pier are included.
Taxis and tricycles can be quite expensive because of the distance, so negotiate the price before you set off.
If you are not confident on a scooter, a car with a driver or a tour package is safer.

items.title: From Del Carmen Pier to the lagoon

children.text: Choose a boat and pay at the ticket area. The boat runs about
20–40 minutes
through the mangroves.
Reviews say the first boat leaves around 8 a.m., and the queue can get long.
Plastic bottles and other single-use plastic reportedly must be handled before boarding, so it is best not to bring them.

The water looks its best from the dry season to just before the rains. One travel blog lists March–October as the period with good weather. In the rainy season the sea in Siargao can turn rough and boats may stop running, so leave a spare day in your schedule.

Early morning is the best time of day. On the first boat you can avoid the queue at the jump platform and the crowds, and your photos of the water come out cleaner. On weekends, holidays and in peak season, boats crowd in from the morning.
The lagoon closes for environmental maintenance from mid-January to early February in some years, so avoid this period or confirm before you plan.

General Luna is the most convenient place to stay. Near the surf spot Cloud 9 there are many choices from hostels to beach resorts, and there are also small places close to the lagoon on the Del Carmen side. To catch the first boat at dawn you need to leave General Luna early, so settle your lodging and transport the day before.

Reviews disagree: some say the lagoon has almost no food, while others say the floating house sells food and water. Bring snacks and water, and have lunch near the pier, at the eatery on Kawhagan Sandbar, or in General Luna. At Kawhagan, Filipino home cooking such as pork adobo and grilled fish is reported from about
If you arrive on the first boat, you can enjoy the jump platform and photos at a relaxed pace.
The boat fee is per boat, so gathering a group from your accommodation to fill the boat makes it much cheaper.
Bring plenty of cash in pesos. Tables, kayaks, life jackets and meals are mostly paid in cash.
Wear water shoes, since there may be coral or sharp rocks.
Bring a waterproof pouch, sunscreen and a hat. The mangrove channels have shade, but the sun is strong at the lagoon.
Reportedly, single-use plastic must be left behind or sorted before boarding. Use a reusable bottle.
If you fly a drone, Kawhagan Sandbar is a popular filming spot. Check the rules locally.
Tour packages on booking sites can cost more than choosing a boat at the pier yourself, but pickup and logistics are easier.

Sugba Lagoon reportedly closes for about 32 days every year (usually mid-January to early February) as a "tourist holiday" for environmental maintenance, under a 2019 Del Carmen ordinance. In 2025 it ran January 10 to February 10, and in 2026 the municipality announced the reopening on February 10 after a month-long break (start dates differ between reports). The mangrove forest, Kawhagan Sandbar and Pamomo-an Beach reportedly stay open during that time. Dates and fees change every year, so check with the Del Carmen tourism office or your operator before you go.
The stay in the lagoon can be limited to about 3 hours per group. Keep to the time.
At the jump platform, check the water depth and any underwater obstacles, and do not jump after drinking or with young children.
In the rainy season or during typhoons, boats may not run because of waves, so leave slack in your schedule.
If you travel by scooter, carry an international driver's license and a helmet, and be careful on wet roads.
In peak season the jump platform queue and the floating house get crowded, so always leave your belongings where staff are present.
Tidal pools on Siargao's eastern coast, on the opposite side from Del Carmen, so people usually visit them on a separate day. Swimming is possible only at low tide, so check the tide.
The classic island-hopping trip from General Luna. It works well to plan it on a separate day from the Sugba Lagoon trip.
